items.followUp: State the fixed points and number of divisions on the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales.

rubric.why: Identifies the Celsius scale’s fixed points and interval divisions.
rubric.description: Celsius scale: fixed points and divisions
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the ice and steam points (0°C and 100°C) and 1 mark for stating that the interval is divided into 100 equal parts.

rubric.why: Identifies the Fahrenheit scale’s fixed points and interval divisions.
rubric.description: Fahrenheit scale: fixed points and divisions
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the ice and steam points (32°F and 212°F) and 1 mark for stating that the interval is divided into 180 equal parts.

modelAnswer: The Celsius scale has two fixed points: the ice point is 0°C and the steam point is 100°C.
The interval between these points is divided into 100 equal divisions.
Figure (Celsius): 100°C — steam point; 100 equal divisions; 0°C — ice point.
The Fahrenheit scale has two fixed points: the ice point is 32°F and the steam point is 212°F.
The interval between these points is divided into 180 equal divisions.
Figure (Fahrenheit): 212°F — steam point; 180 equal divisions; 32°F — ice point.

items.followUp: A hollow metal cube has a side of 4 cm, a mass of 180 g and is made of metal of density 3 g cm⁻³. Find the volume of its cavity.

rubric.why: Shows the relevant data in consistent units.
rubric.how: Award the mark for using the stated mass, side and density consistently; SI values are 0.306 kg, 0.05 m and 2550 kg/m³.
Award the mark for calculating side cubed.

rubric.why: Uses density to find the volume of the glass itself.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using ρ=m/V or V=m/ρ and 1 mark for the correct glass volume.

rubric.why: Subtracts the glass volume from the cube’s total volume to obtain the cavity volume.
rubric.how: Award the mark for the correct difference and answer with a volume unit.

modelAnswer: Given: side = 5 cm = 0.05 m, mass of glass = 306 g = 0.306 kg, density of glass = 2.55 g cm⁻³ = 2550 kg m⁻³.
Volume of cube = side³.
Volume of cube = (0.05 m)³ = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ m³.
Density = mass ÷ volume, so volume of glass = mass ÷ density.
Volume of glass = (0.306 kg) ÷ (2550 kg m⁻³) = 1.20 × 10⁻⁴ m³.
Volume of cavity = volume of cube − volume of glass.
Volume of cavity = 1.25 × 10⁻⁴ m³ − 1.20 × 10⁻⁴ m³ = 5.0 × 10⁻⁶ m³ = 5 cm³.

items.followUp: Differentiate between atomic physics and particle physics.

rubric.why: States the subject matter of atomic physics.
rubric.how: Award the mark for explaining that atomic physics studies atoms, particularly their structure or the behaviour of electrons outside the nucleus.

rubric.why: States the subject matter of nuclear physics.
rubric.how: Award the mark for explaining that nuclear physics studies the nucleus, its structure or nuclear reactions.

modelAnswer: Atomic physics deals with the structure and properties of atoms, especially the behaviour of electrons outside the nucleus.
Nuclear physics deals with the structure and properties of the atomic nucleus and the reactions that take place in it.

items.followUp: Give one example each of a base quantity and a derived quantity.

rubric.why: Defines base quantities as independent quantities.
rubric.how: Award the mark for stating that base quantities are independent and are not defined in terms of other physical quantities.

rubric.why: Defines derived quantities in relation to base quantities.
rubric.how: Award the mark for stating that derived quantities are obtained by combining base quantities.

modelAnswer: Base quantities are independent physical quantities and are not defined in terms of other physical quantities.
Derived quantities are obtained by combining two or more base quantities.

items.followUp: A screw gauge has a pitch of 0.5 mm and 50 divisions on its circular scale. Calculate its least count.

rubric.how: Award the mark for writing least count = pitch ÷ number of divisions on the circular scale.

rubric.why: Identifies the quantities used in the formula.
rubric.how: Award the mark for correctly identifying the pitch and the number of circular-scale divisions.

modelAnswer: Least count of a screw gauge = pitch of the screw ÷ number of divisions on its circular scale.

items.followUp: A person walks 3 m east and then 4 m west. Find the distance travelled and the displacement.

rubric.why: Distinguishes distance as the total path length and a scalar quantity.
rubric.how: Award the mark for defining distance as the total length of the path travelled, without direction.

rubric.why: Distinguishes displacement as a directed change in position.
rubric.how: Award the mark for defining displacement as the shortest straight-line distance from initial to final position, with direction.

modelAnswer: Distance is the total length of the actual path travelled; it is a scalar quantity.
Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from the initial position to the final position, with direction; it is a vector quantity.

items.followUp: What is meant by zero acceleration?

rubric.why: Describes positive acceleration as an increase in velocity with time.
rubric.how: Award the mark for stating that velocity increases with time.

rubric.why: Describes negative acceleration as a decrease in velocity with time or acceleration opposite to the velocity.
rubric.how: Award the mark for either correct description of negative acceleration.

modelAnswer: Positive acceleration occurs when the velocity of an object increases with time.
Negative acceleration occurs when the velocity of an object decreases with time; it acts opposite to the direction of velocity.

items.followUp: A body of mass 3 kg moves with a velocity of 4 m s⁻¹. Calculate its momentum.

rubric.why: Gives the definition or formula for momentum.
rubric.how: Award the mark for stating that momentum is the product of mass and velocity.

rubric.why: Gives the correct SI unit of momentum.
rubric.how: Award the mark for the SI unit kilogram metre per second, equivalent to newton second.

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of the mass of a body and its velocity: p = mv.
Momentum is a vector quantity.
Its SI unit is kg m s⁻¹ (or N s).
